message.reasoning:
I am ready to play Monopoly as an AI player.

I have $707 and no monopolies. p2 has $831 and is close to completing the red group. p3 has $704 and owns Baltic and Vermont. I am weighing whether to trade or mortgage.

p3 also owns Connecticut, St Charles Place, States Avenue, and Ventnor. He needs Oriental from p4 for the light blue group and Virginia for the pink group. The yellow group is split three ways. p4 has $1028 and owns Reading Railroad, Oriental, St James Place, Atlantic Avenue, and Park Place.

Mortgaging is not worthwhile with $707 in cash. I am now considering a trade proposal, since p2 still needs my Kentucky to complete the red group.

I rejected p2's Boardwalk offer for Kentucky. That trade would not complete a set for me. I cannot easily build monopolies either. The orange group needs both St. James and New York Avenue. The red group needs Indiana and Illinois from p2, which is too expensive.

No simple one-for-one trade would complete a monopoly for me without also completing one for another player. p3 is closest to finishing his pink group, since Virginia Avenue is unowned and he needs it to complete the set.

Multi-party trades are unavailable. I am considering a deal with p4 for something useful, but I will not sell Tennessee Avenue to them. Once New York Avenue is purchased, p4 would be one trade away from completing the orange group.

I cannot trade for St. James from p4 because they require a completed monopoly in return, which I cannot offer. Ventnor from p3 would still leave me needing Atlantic Avenue. Water Works and Short Line are too low-value to trade.

I will end the turn. No trade is worth the risk of handing out a monopoly or weakening my blockers.

I am reconsidering the red group. If p2 completes it with houses, the rent would be severe. I am checking exact rent values for Indiana, Kentucky, and Illinois.

Exact red group rent values confirm the danger. Indiana, Kentucky, and Illinois each charge $18–$20 for one house and $100–$300 for two. With $831, p2 could build two houses on each property immediately. I will never trade Kentucky unless I receive something that bankrupts them or gives me an equal or better monopoly right away. A deal for Indiana and Illinois in exchange for Kentucky is impossible because p2 would demand a completed monopoly in return.

I rejected a bad offer to trade Kentucky for Indiana and Illinois because it would waste a trade exchange. I am now considering offering Marvin Gardens for Atlantic Avenue from p4.

I rejected the trade for Atlantic Avenue from p4 because it would give them two yellows and leave me needing Ventnor. I also dismissed swapping Tennessee for St. James Place since neither side would complete a set. I will end the turn.
